about.title: Mendota Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Mendota is a small, close-knit agricultural community, but that doesn't mean property owners get a pass when hazards go unaddressed. Whether the fall happened at a grocery store off Derrick Avenue, a rental unit near Oller Street, or a business fronting Rt 33, California law asks the same core question: did the owner know, or should they have known, about the dangerous condition, and did they fail to fix or warn about it? That's called notice, and it's the heart of most premises cases here. Because Mendota is a compact town, surveillance footage from local businesses often gets overwritten within days, so acting quickly to preserve it matters. LawProactive doesn't practice law or promise outcomes — we simply connect you, at no cost, with an independent attorney who can evaluate the hazard, the notice issue, and your options under a contingency fee arrangement, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Independent Attorney First

items.title: Notice Is Everything
items.desc: California requires proof the property owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard and didn't fix or warn about it. An attorney can help identify evidence, like prior complaints or inspection logs, that establishes that notice.

items.title: Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many Mendota businesses recycle surveillance footage within days or weeks. An attorney can send a preservation request quickly so critical video isn't lost.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't Bar Your Claim
items.desc: Even if you were partly distracted or moving quickly when you fell, California's pure comparative fault rule still allows you to recover a reduced amount. An attorney can help present the facts fairly.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Mendota?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a public entity, such as a city building or school, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim. It's best to have an attorney review the specifics as soon as possible.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for not seeing the hazard?
items.answer: California follows pure comparative fault, so being partly responsible doesn't automatically prevent you from recovering compensation. Your recovery may simply be reduced by your percentage of fault. An attorney can help sort out how fault is likely to be allocated in your specific situation.

items.question: Does it matter that Mendota is a small town with fewer big businesses?
items.answer: Not really — the same premises liability rules apply whether the fall happened at a small local shop near Rt 33 or a larger retailer. What matters most is whether the property owner had notice of the hazard and failed to address it. Smaller businesses may have less formal inspection records, which can actually help or complicate a claim depending on the facts.

items.question: Do I have to pay anything to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free connection service, and the independent attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no cost or obligation to have your situation reviewed.
